mrb_bint_new_str passes the string and length directly to mpz_init_set_str. If x starts with '-', the bug is triggered.
For IREP_TT_BIGINT pool loading, s[0] is the length byte. If s[0] > 127, it becomes negative when cast to mrb_int, causing negative len in mpz_init_set_str.

note: For bigint literals with plen > 127, buf[0] becomes negative as signed char. This negative length is later used in vm.c to call mrb_bint_new_str with a negative len.
With negative len (e.g., -56), i starts at -57 and decrements further, reading s[-57], s[-58], etc., which is an out-of-bounds read before the string buffer - potentially a heap-use-after-free.

code: if (*s == '-') { sn = -1; s++; } else if (base < 0) { sn = -1; base = -base; }
note: For negative bigint literals, base is 0x80 (-128), so base < 0 branch is taken, setting sn=-1 and base=128. The *s=='-' branch is not taken because digits are stored without the sign.
The primary trigger is a bigint literal with >127 digits, causing s[0] (length byte) to be negative, leading to negative len and out-of-bounds reads before the buffer.
